description: How the pandemic turned Peloton into a trillion-dollar dream — then crushed it — while apparel and budget gyms quietly won. Market-cap race (2007–2026) showing the boom, the recall, and the survivor plays.
youtube_description:
Timeline race: Peloton's rocket launch (IPO 2019) → pandemic peak (2020–21) → treadmill recall, supply hangover and reopenings that crashed a superstar. Meanwhile Lululemon's Mirror bet (2020) and apparel dominance converted a lot of at-home demand into sustainable apparel margins; Planet Fitness rode a value-gym rebound; Nike kept growing via brand and direct-to-consumer.

This video animates 2007–2026 market caps in billions USD so you can see the drama frame-by-frame: a sudden vertical spike, a catastrophic fall, and steady winners creeping past.

Sources: company market-cap snapshots, filings, and major financial reporting on IPOs, Peloton recall (2021), Lululemon’s Mirror acquisition (2020), and public market data through 2026.

Like, subscribe and hit the bell for more chart-race breakdowns. Comment which moment shocked you the most — Peloton’s peak or the wipeout?
